Direct adjacency inspection retains the stated threshold-region discontinuities from point_index 447 to 466 for InAlAs and 363 to 382 for InGaAs. Requiring exact ledger reproduction as a pre-implementation stop gate is sufficient; embedding hundreds of row identities in the plan is unnecessary.
findings.statement: Exact row identities, shared-group provenance, and point-index adjacency are available from the bound tables, and the plan's no-bridging rule uniquely determines the finite and excluded-row ledgers before implementation.

findings.rationale: Each b_g is the maximum departure when group g is perturbed and all other groups remain nominal. For nonlinear square roots, minima, ratios, absolute relative changes, and threshold-dependent categories, interaction terms can make a simultaneous multi-group departure larger than the sum of departures measured only at the nominal background. Summation is a valid enclosing argument only if each group bound is uniform over all admissible settings of the other groups, or if the calculation uses another verified enclosure method. The current validation check confirms arithmetic completeness but not enclosure.
findings.statement: The additive one-group-at-a-time construction does not generally enclose simultaneous admissible perturbations of the nonlinear decision metrics, so its endpoints cannot yet serve as deterministic robustness bounds for support or rejection.

findings.rationale: Whole-profile finite-mask error uses both material-resolved profiles, while contiguous support length addresses the front/tail contrast without interpolating gaps. The plan limits claims to the frozen constant-D, constant-boundary family and defers microscopic mechanism separation under explicit adequacy and stability conditions. Four factorial cells and four tightened reruns are low-cost and reuse outputs across masks. Fresh exact-source domain review and initialization are correctly required because execution_context supplies no capability evidence and the visible historical initialization is differently keyed.
findings.statement: The current selection covers both original mandatory observables for this bounded experiment, preserves the later mechanism-comparison closure condition, and uses a proportionate eight-case design whose execution feasibility remains explicitly conditional.

global_confounders: Pixel-digitized observations are not author raw SIMS measurements, and all-zero detection-limit flags conflict with some central concentrations at or below 3e15 cm^-3.
Material identity remains paired with its paper-reported material-specific diffusion coefficient, restricting causal claims to the declared phenomenological family.
The current sensitivity calculation does not establish enclosure under simultaneous perturbation of multiple dependence groups.
Backend feasibility is not independently established by execution_context and depends on the declared fresh domain review and initialization gates.

confounders: The G decision combines nonlinear WRMSE, root-mean-square, minimum, and ratio operations for which nominal one-group departures do not guarantee a simultaneous-perturbation bound.
Material and fixed material-specific D remain paired, so conclusions apply only within the frozen anchor family.

hypothesis_reviews.smallest_resolving_action: Retain the finite masks and exact no-gap T definition, but compute a verified deterministic enclosure for T and relative-T over the declared perturbation set, or narrow the support/rejection rule to the explicitly tested one-group-at-a-time scenarios.

next_actions: Revise the deterministic envelope definition so each component bound is uniform over other admissible group settings, or use a verified interval enclosure for WRMSE, J, G, T, and relative T.

If retaining the current nominal one-group calculation, call it a sensitivity score, define its perturbation set explicitly, and remove any claim that its endpoints bound simultaneous digitization uncertainty.

After that bounded correction, run the already declared exact reference-ledger audit and fresh domain review/initialization before implementation or execution; retain later microscopic mechanism work under the existing conditions.
payload.summary: The revision resolves the finite-log-uncertainty blocker: direct recomputation from the bound row tables gives M0 counts 359/702, M1 383/753, and M2 439/757 for InAlAs/InGaAs, with S0 373/702, S1 397/755, and S2 501/765 and excluded counts 14/0, 14/2, and 62/8. The exact row identities are present and the no-missing-index adjacency rule is executable, including the documented 447-to-466 and 363-to-382 gaps. The original objective and both mandatory observables are covered within a bounded constant-D boundary counterfactual, while microscopic mechanism separation and stronger empirical claims remain properly conditional later work. The four physical cells plus four convergence reruns are proportionate, and feasibility is correctly gated because the supplied execution context does not independently establish backend capability. However, the replacement additive sensitivity interval is not generally an enclosing deterministic bound: each b_g is evaluated with every other group nominal, so nonlinear interaction under simultaneous group perturbations can exceed the sum of nominal one-group departures. Because G and relative-T support/rejection use those endpoints as robustness gates, this is material to identifiability. The smallest correction is a rigorous enclosing deterministic calculation over the declared perturbation set, such as verified interval propagation or bounded differences uniform over the other admissible coordinates; alternatively, label the current quantity as a one-group-at-a-time sensitivity score and cease using it to claim robustness outside that tested set. No additional TCAD cases or probabilistic uncertainty system are required.
